projection: south polar stereographic, sphere 1737.4 km, true scale at the pole: rho = 2R*tan((90+lat)/2), x = rho*sin(lon) (towards 90 E), y = rho*cos(lon) (towards 0 E); image row 0 is y max, column 0 is x min
value: share of time any part of the solar disc is visible, 0..1; grey = 255*sqrt(value)
source: NASA LOLA average illumination map AVGVISIB_75S_120M_201608 (PGDA, Mazarico et al. 2011), 18.6-year average, 120 m pixels averaged to 240 m
